headline: TRACE reports accountable retrieval gains on one OCR-degraded French historical archive benchmark
summary: Bian et al. introduce TRACE, a training-free agentic retrieval system designed for OCR-degraded, heterogeneous historical archives. On HistoriQA-ThirdRepublic, 1,752 French-language questions over BnF-derived parliamentary debates and newspapers from 1887, the authors report overall R@10 0.856 and multi-gold MRR 0.653, above tested BM25, dense, graph-based and agentic RAG baselines. Its components include corpus-targeted query decomposition, fused sparse/dense/temporal retrieval, explicit accept/reject/hold verdicts with deferred re-evaluation, and cross-sub-question reranking. The paper reports roughly $0.02 per question under its hosted-inference configuration and an internal project prototype accessible to 24 researchers across six institutions. These are author-reported results on one corpus; code was not run, and adoption, expert workload, trust and transfer beyond the 1887 French setting remain unmeasured.
